name: Regime-Routed (KL-UCB / LinTS / DTS+PH)
tagline: Routes by regime: KL-UCB if K>5 stationary, LinTS if contextual, dual-rate discounted Thompson Sampling with two-sided Page-Hinkley soft-reset on K≤5 nonstationary.

key_hyperparams.name: burst_length
key_hyperparams.role: steps of fast discount after detected change

key_hyperparams.name: soft_reset decay
key_hyperparams.role: fraction of mass kept after soft reset

key_hyperparams.name: min_n for PH
key_hyperparams.role: minimum arm pulls before PH triggers

init_recovers: KL-UCB on stationary, LinTS on contextual
diff_from_baseline: Versus the three baselines, builds an explicit regime router: KL-UCB on big-K stationary, LinTS contextual, and a discounted-Thompson policy with two-sided Page-Hinkley + dual-rate decay (slow γ then fast γ for burst_length steps after detected change) for small-K nonstationary.

name: Discounted KL-UCB + LinUCB
tagline: KL-UCB using both full and discounted statistics (switches at t>1000) plus a LinUCB head for the contextual case.
formula: $$N_a^{(d)} \leftarrow \gamma N_a^{(d)} + \mathbf{1}[\text{pull}=a],\ S_a^{(d)} \leftarrow \gamma S_a^{(d)} + r\cdot\mathbf{1}[\cdot],\ \gamma = 0.995,$$ $$n_{\mathrm{eff}} = N_a^{(d)}\,\tfrac{1-\gamma}{1-\gamma^{N_a^{(d)}}},\quad U_a = \sup\{q : n_{\mathrm{eff}}\,\mathrm{kl}(\hat\mu^{(d)}_a, q) \le \log t\}\ (t > 1000),$$ $$\mathrm{LinUCB:}\ \theta_a = A_a^{-1} b_a,\ U_a = \theta_a^\top x + \sqrt{2\log(t+1)\cdot x^\top A_a^{-1} x}.$$

key_hyperparams.name: switch threshold
key_hyperparams.role: use discounted stats only after this

init_recovers: KL-UCB at t ≤ 1000; standard LinUCB on contextual
diff_from_baseline: Versus KL-UCB / LinUCB baselines, maintains discounted parallel statistics (γ=0.995) and switches the index from full-history KL-UCB to discounted KL-UCB with effective sample size after t = 1000; contextual case is plain LinUCB.

name: KL-UCB + Multi-Window GLR Reset (LinTS contextual)
tagline: KL-UCB on per-arm reward histories with a multi-window Bernoulli GLR change-detector that triggers a hard era reset; contextual case uses eigh-based LinTS.
init_recovers: KL-UCB on stationary, LinTS on contextual when no GLR fires
diff_from_baseline: Versus KL-UCB, attaches a multi-scale Bernoulli GLR test on the most-recently-pulled arm's history (windows 20/50/100/200, threshold 12) that hard-resets the era_t and full history on detection; contextual uses LinTS with very tight v² = 0.01.

name: Regime-Routed Memory Fusion
tagline: Three internal heads — small-K stationary uses KL-UCB blended with sliding-window KL-UCB; nonstationary uses drift-gated long+short Thompson; contextual uses optimistic LinUCB with mild noise.
init_recovers: KL-UCB on small-K (when local window empty); LinUCB-like on contextual
diff_from_baseline: Versus KL-UCB / Thompson / LinUCB baselines, fuses long- and short-memory statistics in three different ways depending on regime: blended KL-UCB for small-K (with periodic hard reset), drift-gated TS-fusion for big-K nonstationary, and optimistic LinUCB with decaying optimism + small Gaussian noise for contextual.
